steps.prompt: $471$: add its digits. Now try dividing $471$ by $3$. What do you notice?

cards.title: Add the digits
cards.body: A number divides by $3$ exactly when its digit sum does, and the same for $9$. $471$: $4 + 7 + 1 = 12$, and $12$ divides by $3$, so $471$ does too ($471 = 3 \times 157$). Even better: the remainder of the number is the remainder of its digit sum.

cards.title: Worked example: remainder by 9
cards.problem: What is the remainder when $583$ is divided by $9$?

try.prompt: What is the remainder when $16$ is divided by $9$?

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: $10 = 9 + 1$, $100 = 99 + 1$, $1000 = 999 + 1$. So $583 = 5 \times 99 + 8 \times 9 + (5 + 8 + 3)$. The $99$s and $9$s divide by $9$ (and by $3$), so only the digit sum is left.

prompts: Explain in your own words why the digit-sum test works for $9$.
